title: 参观工厂 · The Factory Tour
desc: What you see on a Chinese factory tour and what to ask about it: workshops, lines, warehouses, inspection points, certifications, and the questions that show whether the factory really makes your product.

title: 出行 · Getting Around: Rail, Didi, and Paying
desc: The logistics of a factory trip: high-speed rail tickets on a passport, hailing a Didi to an industrial zone, paying by phone, and checking into a hotel.

title: 饭局 · The Business Banquet
desc: A condensed script for the dinner after a factory visit: seating, the first toast, declining drinks without offence, the toast you give back, and leaving well.

title: 工厂 · Factory Words: Samples, Tooling, and QC
desc: The working vocabulary of a Chinese factory floor, in the order a product moves through it: 打样, 封样, 开模, 大货, 验货, 出货.

title: 合同 · Contracts, Seals, and IP
desc: The contract vocabulary a buyer needs at a Chinese factory: which language governs, which seal binds, NNN agreements, patents and trademarks, tooling ownership, penalties, and arbitration.

title: 会谈 · The Meeting Room
desc: The phrases that keep a foreign buyer in control of a factory meeting: titles, openings, clarifying, pinning down commitments, and decoding a polite no.

title: 水杯 · How a Bottle Is Made
desc: The process vocabulary of a drinkware factory: forming and welding a stainless vacuum bottle, how the vacuum is made and tested, lids and plastic parts, glass, food-contact standards, and custom branding.

title: 谈价 · Price, Payment, and Numbers
desc: The money half of a factory negotiation: reading a quotation, tax and invoices, trade terms, deposits and balances, haggling lines, and the numbers that trip learners up.

title: 投诉 · Quality Complaints and Claims
desc: How to raise a quality problem with a Chinese factory firmly without costing anyone face: reporting the defect, demanding a root cause and 8D report, and negotiating who pays.

title: 微信 · WeChat and Written Follow-up
desc: Where a factory relationship lives after the visit: adding contacts, the thank-you message, meeting minutes, chasing progress, and handling voice messages.

title: 商务 · Visiting a Chinese Factory: A Reading Path
desc: The business Chinese for a buyer's factory visit, in the order you will need it: the meeting, the floor, the product, the price, the contract, problems, the tour, the dinner, and the follow-up.

title: 都 · 每 · 所有 · quantifiers
desc: All, every, some, many, none: 都 carries the whole system, and the other quantifiers lean on it.

title: 时态 · past, present, future
desc: Mandarin verbs never change form: time words, 了, 过, 着, 在, and 会 do the work English does with conjugation.

title: 古琴 · the scholar's zither
desc: The seven-string zither Confucius played throughout his life, and the origin of 知音, the word for a person who truly understands you.

title: 生旦净末丑 · Role Types in Peking Opera
desc: The five 行当 of Peking Opera: sheng, dan, jing, mo, and chou, each a lifelong specialization in voice, movement, and makeup.

title: 诗经 · Book of Songs
desc: The 305 poems of China's oldest anthology (c. 1046-600 BCE), which Confucius said no educated person could afford to ignore.

title: 书法风格 · The Five Scripts of Chinese Calligraphy
desc: The five scripts of Chinese calligraphy, 篆隶楷行草, run from Zhou bronze inscriptions to Tang wild cursive; choosing a script is choosing a register.

title: 宋词 · Song Dynasty Lyric
desc: Song lyrics (词 cí) fit fixed tune patterns called 词牌; Li Qingzhao, Su Shi, and Xin Qiji are the form's three masters.

title: 道 · way, path
desc: The character that opens the Dàodéjīng and names Daoism: way, path, principle, and the measure word for rivers and light.

title: 和 · harmony, and, with; peace
desc: 禾 (grain) beside 口 (mouth): 和 is both Mandarin's everyday "and" and the Confucian ideal of harmony without uniformity.

title: 快 · fast, happy
desc: 快 joins 忄 (heart) to 夬 (a decisive cut): speed and joy are the same image, a heart running without drag.

title: 人 · person, humanity
desc: Two strokes, barely changed since the oracle bones, write 人 rén; add 二 and you get 仁, Confucian benevolence.

title: 为 · to do; to act; for; because of
desc: In oracle bone script 为 is a hand leading an elephant, and it sits at the center of Daoist 无为 non-action.

title: 玉 · jade, precious
desc: Three jade discs on a cord, one dot away from 王 (wáng, king): the stone Confucius said was virtue made visible.

title: 了 · the perfective particle
desc: Post-verb 了 marks a completed action; sentence-final 了 announces a new situation, and the two can stack in one sentence.

title: 量词 · measure words
desc: 个, 只, 条, 本, 张: the classifier taxonomy and the logic behind it.

title: 乃 · classical connective: then, thereupon, thus; to be; only then
desc: Classical 乃 marks a consequence as earned, where modern 就 stays neutral; as emphatic copula it gives 失败乃成功之母 its weight.

title: 之 · classical genitive, nominalizer, and pronoun
desc: 之 zhī did the work of 'of', 'him/her/it', and 'the one who' in classical Chinese; it survives in 之间, 之后, and 总之.

title: 者 · classical nominalizer "the one who; that which"
desc: 者 zhě turns any verb into "the one who": 学者 scholar, 读者 reader, 作者 author, unchanged since the Analects.

title: 科举 · The Imperial Examination System
desc: The exam that selected China's officials for 1,300 years, from the Sui in 605 CE to abolition in 1905.

title: 清朝 · The Qing Dynasty
desc: Invited through Shanhai Pass in 1644, the Manchus ruled China for 268 years, until the 1911 revolution ended imperial rule.

title: 宋朝 · The Song Dynasty
desc: Economic revolution, printing, compass: the dynasty modernity missed.

title: 战国时期 · Warring States Period
desc: Seven states fought from 475 to 221 BCE, and that same fragmentation produced Confucianism, Daoism, Legalism, and Mohism.

title: 儒家 · Confucianism
desc: The school of the ru: ritual, hierarchy, and moral cultivation as state religion.

title: 祖先崇拜 · Ancestor Veneration
desc: Shang oracle bones record divinations to royal ancestors; 祖先崇拜, the ritual care of the dead, continues today in tablets, offerings, and Qingming graves.

title: 轮回 · samsara; the cycle of rebirth
desc: 轮回 renders Sanskrit saṃsāra as 'wheel' plus 'return': the karmic cycle carrying beings through six realms until liberation.

title: 缘分 · karmic connection
desc: Buddhist karmic fate: 500 years of cultivation to share a boat with a stranger, a thousand to share a pillow.

title: 禅 · meditation; Chan; to abdicate
desc: One altar character, two civilizations: read shàn it yields thrones and sacrifices to earth; read chán it transliterates Sanskrit dhyāna and founds Zen.

title: 星 · star; celestial body; spark
desc: Born of the sun radical and a sprout, 星 names the stars, the planets, the week, movie fame, and the spark that starts prairie fires.

title: 电脑与网络 · Computers & the Internet
desc: The computer is an electric brain, downloading is "carrying down," and the number 666 is a compliment.

title: 度量衡 · Weights & Measures
desc: Fruit is priced by the half-kilo 斤, distance walks in 里, and an idiom about six of one and half a dozen still counts in base sixteen.

title: 看病 · Seeing a Doctor
desc: Getting sick in Chinese starts with a queue number, runs on the verb "look," and ends with the eternal prescription: drink more hot water.

title: 生意 · Doing Business
desc: Business in Chinese is literally "the meaning of life," merchants are named after a fallen dynasty, and the deal closes at the dinner table.

title: 数字系统 · The Chinese Number System
desc: Chinese numbers are built from eleven syllables and zero irregularity; the catch is that the system pivots on ten thousand, not one thousand.

title: 天气 · Talking About the Weather
desc: Rain falls, wind blows, and fog counts as a noun-verb drama: the small grammar of weather is a beginner's best conversation opener.

title: 结果补语 · resultative complements
desc: Chinese verbs describe the attempt; a second syllable reports the outcome. Listening is 听, but understanding what you heard is 听懂.

title: 可能补语 · potential complements
desc: Slide 得 or 不 inside a verb-result pair and it states ability: 听懂 is understood, 听得懂 is can understand, 听不懂 is the learner's anthem.

title: 离合词 · separable verbs
desc: Words that unzip: 见面 is to meet, but meeting him is 跟他见面 and meeting once is 见一次面, because the "word" is secretly verb plus object.

title: 又 · 再 · again, twice over
desc: Chinese has two agains: 又 looks backward at a repetition that happened, 再 looks forward to one still to come. 再见 is the proof.

title: 正反问 · A-not-A questions
desc: Chinese asks yes-no questions by offering both answers: 去不去 is "going, not going?", and the pattern replaces 吗 with built-in neutrality.

title: 工程 · Engineering
desc: From the carpenter's square inside 工 to the high-speed rail map, the vocabulary of a civilization that has always thought in projects.

title: 化学 · Chemistry
desc: The Chinese periodic table is a naming machine: one character per element, with the radical telling you its state at room temperature.

title: 生物 · Biology & the Naming of Living Things
desc: The panda is a bear-cat, the giraffe a long-necked deer, and the word for gene may be the best translation in the language.

title: 数学 · Mathematics
desc: The vocabulary of Chinese mathematics, where calculus is "tiny accumulation" and geometry was named by a Ming official translating Euclid.

title: 天文 · Astronomy
desc: The five visible planets are named for the five phases, comets are brooms, and the space program borrows its names from mythology.

title: 物理 · Physics
desc: Physics in Chinese is "the pattern of things," a phrase lifted from a Song-dynasty program for investigating the world.

title: 多少 · how much, how many
desc: Chinese builds its "how much" by welding many to few, part of a system where opposites fuse into the scale between them.

title: 高兴 · happy, glad
desc: Happiness as elevation: spirits that rise. The everyday glad word, and how it divides the territory with 开心, 快乐, and 幸福.

title: 考试 · examination
desc: China ran the world's longest experiment in testing, thirteen centuries of imperial exams, and the vocabulary still sits every June for the gaokao.

title: 明白 · to understand; clear
desc: Understanding as illumination: sun-and-moon brightness plus plain white. The clarity verb, and its siblings 懂, 知道, and 了解.

title: 声音 · sound; voice
desc: A chime-stone struck beside an ear: the word for sound welds raw noise to patterned tone, and Chinese theory kept the two distinct.

title: 身体 · body; health
desc: The word for body doubles as the word for health, asking about it is a greeting, and its second character got luckier in simplification than any other.

title: 小人 · the petty person
desc: Confucius took a word that meant "commoner" and turned it into the permanent opposite of the gentleman: the small-hearted schemer of every office.

title: 音乐 · music
desc: Music and joy share a single character, a soulmate is "the one who knows your tone," and the zither smashed for a dead friend still echoes.

title: 医院 · hospital
desc: The healing courtyard: how an arrow wound, a wine jar, and the institutional suffix 院 assembled the word for hospital.

title: 饱 · full, satisfied, to eat one's fill
desc: The food radical 饣 wraps the sound of 包 (bāo), so the glyph itself is a stomach packed full like a dumpling.

title: 报 · to report, to announce; newspaper; to repay
desc: A hand cuffing a kneeling criminal once meant sentencing; today the same glyph carries newspapers, reports, and the moral arithmetic of repayment.

title: 病 · illness, disease, to fall ill, fault
desc: A person sweating on a sickbed with the phonetic 丙 inside: the radical 疒 frames every Chinese word for being unwell.

title: 草 · grass, herb, straw; draft, rough
desc: A field of grass under the morning sun: the grass radical over 早 zǎo (early) gives the plant its sound, and from the meadow grow the senses of herb, straw, and a hasty rough draft.

title: 唱 · to sing, to chant, to call out
desc: A mouth beside the sun-doubled 昌: the radical names the act of singing while 昌 carries only the sound.

title: 穿 · to pierce, to bore through, to wear, to put on
desc: A tooth gnawing through the roof of a cave: one image for boring a hole and for the body slipping into clothing.

title: 船 · ship, boat, vessel
desc: A pictophonetic built on 舟 (boat): the hull carries the meaning while the right side supplies the sound, covering every craft from sampan to ocean liner.

title: 春 · spring, springtime, vitality, the stir of desire
desc: Sun pressing up through young shoots: the season of growth, and the oldest Chinese metaphor for life-force and erotic longing.

title: 错 · error, mistake; wrong, incorrect
desc: A metal character whose oldest sense was inlay and grinding; from crossed, interlocking lines it slid to things crossing wrongly, the modern sense of error.

title: 蛋 · egg, egg-shaped thing, scoundrel
desc: A pictophonetic egg: the 虫 radical for small creatures sits under a sound element, and in slang it turns people into scoundrels.

title: 灯 · lamp, lantern, light
desc: A fire radical 火 fused with the sound 丁, naming everything from oil lamps to the red light that stops traffic.

title: 懂 · to understand, to know, to grasp
desc: A heart-radical verb where comprehension is felt, not just decoded: to truly get something is to take it in inwardly.

title: 短 · short, brief; deficient, lacking
desc: An arrow set beside a ritual bean-pot measures the short distance, so 短 builds its meaning of brevity from a comparison of two small lengths.

title: 队 · team, group, band, military unit; measure word for groups
desc: A crowd of people 人 packed against an earthen mound 阝, the image that gives 队 its sense of a formed-up team or column.

title: 房 · building, house, room
desc: A door radical leaning over the phonetic 方: the side-chamber under a roof that grew into every word for house, room, and the family branches that fill them.

title: 飞 · to fly, to dart; high, swift
desc: A single bird caught mid-flap, one outstretched wing and the rising line of its body, frozen at the instant it leaves the ground.

title: 封 · to seal, envelope, to confer (a fief)
desc: A handful of earth heaped over a boundary mound, sealed by hand: 封 ties envelopes, granaries, and feudal grants to the same gesture of closing something off.

title: 富 · rich, wealthy, abundant, to enrich
desc: A full wine jar tucked under a roof: the picture of a household storehouse packed to its rafters with plenty.

title: 父 · father, male elder, household head
desc: A hand gripping a stone axe: the tool of the one who heads the household, drawn as the figure of the father himself.

title: 改 · to alter, to change, to correct, to reform
desc: A hand raises a stick over a kneeling child: 改 is change enforced by correction, not drift, which is why it leans toward fixing what is wrong.

title: 哥 · elder brother, a familiar term for an older young man
desc: Two 可 stacked into one glyph; the doubled phonetic came to carry the warmest word in the family, elder brother.

title: 歌 · song, lyrics; to sing, to chant
desc: The radical 欠 (an open, exhaling mouth) drives the meaning of song, while 哥 supplies the gē sound.

title: 狗 · dog
desc: A pictophonetic glyph where the beast radical 犭supplies the meaning and 句 lends only the sound, naming the most domesticated of animals.

title: 馆 · a public building, hall, shop, establishment
desc: A food-radical building: the eating-house that grew into the library, the museum, and the embassy.

title: 孩 · baby, child, children
desc: A child-radical fused with the earthly branch 亥: 子 carries the meaning, 亥 lends the rising sound hái.

title: 害 · to harm, injury, calamity, to fear
desc: Under the roof a mouth and a blade build the sense of injury done; the same glyph also means to fear, as in 害怕.

title: 喝 · to drink; (hè) to shout, to cry out
desc: A mouth radical paired with the phonetic 曷, splitting cleanly into the everyday hē you drink with and the older hè you shout with.

title: 河 · river, the Yellow River
desc: 河 began as the personal name of one river, the Yellow River, before it widened to mean any river at all.

title: 湖 · lake, the provinces around Dongting
desc: A water radical against the phonetic 胡, naming every still inland water from West Lake to the jianghu of wandering swordsmen.

title: 坏 · bad, rotten, spoiled; to break down
desc: A picto-phonetic built from 土 earth and 不 not: spoiled soil that yields nothing, extended to anything gone bad or broken.

title: 换 · to change, to exchange, to swap, to trade
desc: A hand verb: every kind of swap, from changing money to changing trains, runs through one moving palm.

title: 黄 · yellow, gold, the imperial color; to fall through
desc: The color of loess soil and the emperor, of the mother river and the egg yolk, and the one color slang that means a plan has collapsed.

title: 活 · to live, to be alive, lively, work
desc: Water gives the verb its life: a stream over a tongue, the flow that means being alive, and from there everything that moves, breathes, and gets done.

title: 鸡 · chicken, fowl, rooster
desc: The simplified 鸡 swaps a chicken-coop hand 又 in where the traditional 雞 kept the sound-bearer 奚 beside the bird.

title: 急 · urgent, anxious, hasty, rapid
desc: A heart pressed from above: 急 stacks a phonetic element over 心, so the glyph itself feels the squeeze of urgency.

title: 价 · price, value, worth
desc: A person standing beside 介 jiè: the worth a thing takes on only once two people sit down to trade for it.

title: 简 · simple, brief, terse; a bamboo writing slip
desc: Before paper, a letter was a strip of bamboo; from that narrow slip 简 grew into the words for simple, brief, and a short note.

title: 接 · to connect, to join, to receive, to meet
desc: The hand that joins: 接 puts a wrist behind every link, every catch, and every arrival you go out to greet.

title: 街 · street, avenue, thoroughfare
desc: The walk radical 行 splits open into a crossroads, and the jade-tablet phonetic 圭 sits inside, marking the place where roads cross and people pass.

title: 姐 · elder sister, miss, young lady
desc: A woman radical fused to the sound-lender 且, 姐 names the elder sister and stretches to cover every miss and young lady in modern address.

title: 借 · to borrow, to lend, to make use of
desc: One glyph carries both halves of a loan: 借 means borrow and lend at once, the direction settled only by context.

title: 紧 · tight, taut, tense, urgent
desc: Thread drawn taut over the silk radical; the same word carries a tight knot, a tense nerve, an urgent deadline, and a tight wallet.

title: 救 · to rescue, to save, to relieve
desc: A hand wields a stick to pull someone out of danger; the phonetic 求 once meant a desperate plea for help.

title: 苦 · bitter, hardship, suffering, painstaking
desc: The grass radical over 古 names a bitter herb on the tongue, then stretches to every flavor of hardship and effort.

title: 困 · to trap, hard-pressed, tired
desc: A tree boxed inside four walls and unable to grow: the picture of being hemmed in, the source of both hardship and sleepiness.

title: 离 · to leave, to be apart, away from
desc: Once the name of a netted mythical bird, 离 was borrowed so long ago for to part that almost no speaker recalls its feathers.

title: 脸 · face, cheeks, social face, reputation
desc: The flesh-radical face that doubles as a ledger of dignity: in Chinese you can lose it, save it, or tear it apart.

title: 练 · to practice, to train, to refine, skilled
desc: Before it meant drilling and rehearsal, 练 was a verb for boiling raw silk soft, the repetition of treatment that hardens into skill.

title: 马 · horse, a common surname
desc: A three-stroke pictograph of a horse in profile that hides the mane, legs, and tail of its towering ancestor 馬.

title: 牛 · ox, cow, cattle; (slang) awesome
desc: A four-stroke pictograph of an ox head seen straight on, the horns still visible; in modern slang it means impressively good.

title: 农 · agriculture, farming, farmer, rural
desc: A character compressed from a graph that showed working the fields at the time of the stars, the whole cycle of growing crops.

title: 朋 · friend, companion; of the same group
desc: Two strings of cowrie shells hung side by side, an old unit of value, borrowed early for companions of equal standing who keep close company.

title: 票 · bank note, ticket, vote, a slip of paper
desc: Flames rising over an altar where spirit money burned: 票 carries the smoke of an offering into the modern banknote, the ticket stub, and the ballot.

title: 热 · hot, heat, fever, ardent, popular
desc: The four dots of flame beneath 执 carry physical heat into the heat of crowds, fervor, and whatever is trending.

title: 肉 · meat, flesh, the pulp of fruit
desc: A pictograph of a meat slab with its marbling drawn inside; squeezed onto the left of a character it becomes 月, the flesh-moon of the body radicals.

title: 送 · to see off, to send, to give
desc: A figure waving 关 at someone whose feet 辶 are already carrying them away: 送 is farewell built into the road itself.

title: 危 · danger, peril, precarious, lofty height
desc: A kneeling figure pinned beneath a cliff overhang spells danger, where the same overhang also carries the sound.

title: 香 · fragrant, delicious, incense, popular
desc: Grain stacked over a mouth of sweetness: 香 is the smell of ripe rice, and the word still means both perfume and a hot meal worth eating.

title: 笑 · to laugh, to smile, to mock
desc: Bamboo over a bending person: a form that has split scholars since the Song over whether laughter or rustling reeds came first.

title: 站 · to stand, to halt, a station, a stop
desc: A person planted upright on the ground, holding their place: from the body that will not move grows the station, the stop, and the website you log on to.

title: 笔 · pen, brush, a stroke, writing
desc: Bamboo over hair: the bamboo-handled writing brush drawn as a character. From the implement grow the act of writing, the strokes that build a glyph, and a measure word for sums and deals.

title: 表 · surface, to express, a table, a watch
desc: The garment radical worn on the outside: 表 runs from the outer surface of things to showing feeling, the chart on a page, and the watch on a wrist.

title: 才 · talent, ability, only-then, not until
desc: A sprout breaking ground, the first sign of growth. From that image grow two threads: talent as raw promise, and the adverb 才 that marks something later, harder, or smaller than expected.

title: 朝 · dynasty, imperial court, to face toward; (zhāo) morning
desc: The sun rising among grasses with the moon still in the sky. From that dawn scene grow two readings: zhāo, the morning and its youthful vigor, and cháo, the court that met at daybreak, the dynasty it served, and the preposition toward.

title: 城 · city, city wall, town
desc: A rampart of earth raised around a settlement: the character where the wall and the city it protects are one and the same word.

title: 传 · to pass on, transmit, spread; (zhuan) a biography, a commentary
desc: The person radical carrying something onward: one figure handing a thing to the next. From that image grow the senses of 传, read chuan when it means to pass down, transmit, and spread, and read zhuan when it names a biography or a classical commentary.

title: 代 · generation, era, to substitute, on behalf of
desc: The person radical carrying the sense of succession: one figure standing in the place of another. From that single image grow the four faces of 代: to replace or act for someone, to do a thing on their behalf, the generation that succeeds the one before, and the era or dynasty in which a life is set.

title: 当 · to be, just at, ought; (dàng) appropriate, to treat as
desc: A high-frequency polyphone with two readings. As dāng it means to serve as, to be at a given time or place, and ought to; as dàng it means appropriate, to treat something as, and to pawn. The tone tells you which sense is in play.

title: 调 · (diào) to transfer, tune, accent; (tiáo) to adjust, to blend, to mediate
desc: A high-frequency polyphone with two readings. As diào it means to transfer, a melody or key, a tone, an accent; as tiáo it means to adjust, to blend, to mediate. The reading tells you whether 调 is moving things or harmonizing them.

title: 定 · to fix, settle, decide, surely
desc: A settling element coming to rest under a roof. From that image of a thing made still and fixed in place grows the whole field of 定: to decide, to set, the fixed and stable, the certain and sure.

title: 而 · and, but, yet (a classical connective)
desc: A pictograph of a beard, borrowed early as one of the busiest function words in literary Chinese. 而 links clause to clause as and, but, or yet, ties manner to verb, and frames set phrases like 而且 and 而已.

title: 发 · to send out, to develop, hair
desc: One simplified glyph that swallowed two traditional characters. 发 carries the fa reading of sending, emitting, and developing (traditional 發) and the fa reading of hair on the head (traditional 髮).

title: 夫 · husband, a grown man, laborer; the literary particle fú
desc: A grown man pictured with a hairpin marking adulthood: the husband and the married couple (丈夫 夫妻 夫人 夫妇), the adult man and laborer (农夫 渔夫 大夫), skill and effort (功夫 工夫), and the classical literary particle 夫 fú that opens a sentence.

title: 公 · public, fair, common, a duke, male
desc: A line dividing away the private self. From that image grow everything held in common, every fair dealing, the metric measures, and the elder male: public, impartial, official, and a duke.

title: 功 · merit, achievement, skill, effort
desc: Merit earned through effort: from meritorious service and success to the patient skill the Chinese call gongfu, and even work in physics.

title: 古 · ancient, old, classical
desc: The mouth radical holding what ten generations have spoken down the years: 古 is what is old because it has been handed on. From that single image grow the senses of antiquity (古代 古老 远古), the classical and the antique (古典 古文 古董 古迹 考古), and the quaint or unconventional (古怪 古板).

title: 故 · reason; old; deliberately; therefore
desc: 故 binds five senses into one glyph: cause, the old and former, deliberateness, the literary "hence," and the deceased. The thread is a settled cause behind what is done or what has passed.

title: 观 · to observe, view, outlook, Daoist temple
desc: The eye that looks and the mind that judges. From watching a thing closely grow two families of meaning: to observe and to view, and the settled outlook through which a person sees the world. A second reading, guàn, names the Daoist temple.

title: 海 · sea, ocean, a vast quantity
desc: Water plus the phonetic 每: the sea, the ocean, and by extension any vastness. From 大海 and 海洋 to the coastal city 上海, the navy 海军, and the crowd that becomes a 人海.

title: 合 · to join, combine, suit, close
desc: A lid closing down over the mouth of a vessel. From that image of two parts meeting and fitting grows the whole field of joining, suiting, closing, and adding up into a whole.

title: 化 · to change, to transform, to melt
desc: The character of transformation itself: melting, digesting, civilizing, and the productive -ize suffix that builds half of modern technical Chinese.

title: 画 · to draw, a painting, a stroke
desc: A hand with a brush drawing the boundaries of a field. From that image grows the whole world of pictures: to paint, a painting, and the single stroke of a character.

title: 己 · oneself, self, the sixth Heavenly Stem
desc: A picture of a coiled, bending thread borrowed long ago to mean the self. From it grows everything turned inward: oneself, the private view, self-restraint, and the sixth of the ten Heavenly Stems.

title: 件 · item, piece, measure word
desc: The measure word for matters, garments, and gifts, and the character behind documents, parts, and cases.

title: 结 · to tie, to unite, to conclude, to bear fruit
desc: A knot tied in silk thread. From that image grows everything that binds and resolves: the knot you tie, the union of two people, the conclusion that settles a matter, and the fruit a plant ties onto its branch.

title: 节 · joint, node, festival, to economize
desc: A bamboo joint, the segment between the knots. From that node grows everything that comes in sections: the joint of a limb, the chapter of a book, the festival that knots the calendar, and the restraint that keeps a thing within bounds.

title: 解 · to untie, to solve, to explain, to dissolve
desc: The character for cutting apart and undoing: untying and liberating, solving and explaining, dissolving and relieving. A polyphone read jiě, jiè, and xiè, pictured as a hand prying an ox horn from the ox.

title: 句 · sentence, phrase, a unit of speech
desc: A wrapping line drawn over a mouth: speech bundled into a single unit. From that image grows the sentence, the line of verse, and the measure word that counts the remarks we say.

title: 乐 · happy, joyful (lè); music (yuè)
desc: A picture of a wooden frame strung with silk and a drum, an early musical instrument. The simplified 乐 carries two readings: yuè for music, the original sense, and lè for joy, the happiness that music gives.

title: 力 · strength, power, force, effort
desc: A picture of a plough or a flexed sinew, the image of bodily exertion. From that one shape grows everything pushed by force: raw strength, the capacity to do, and the effort poured into a task.

title: 历 · to experience, history, calendar
desc: One simplified glyph that absorbed two traditional characters: 歷 (to pass through, history) and 曆 (calendar). The word that holds both lived experience and reckoned time.

title: 连 · to link, to join, even
desc: Carts moving in a line: a character that joins things in space, in sequence, and in emphasis, from 连接 to the famous 连...都 construction.

title: 量 · quantity, capacity; to measure
desc: 商量 shangliang, to discuss, is literally to measure something out together: the act of weighing it between two minds before anyone decides.

title: 论 · to discuss, a theory or treatise
desc: Reasoned speech put in order: the verb for discussing, debating, and commenting, and the noun for a theory, a view, or a treatise. Also Lun in the title of the Analects.

title: 民 · the people, a citizen, folk
desc: The common people as a collective subject: the populace, the citizen, the folk and the nation, and the civilian set against the military. From 人民 the people to 民族 ethnic nation to 民主 democracy.

title: 平 · flat, level, even, peaceful, ordinary
desc: A pictograph of something level and balanced. From that flat surface grows a wide field of meaning: the even and the smooth, the equal and the fair, the calm and the peaceful, and the plain and ordinary.

title: 清 · clear, clean, pure, quiet
desc: Water beside the color of new growth. The character that names limpid water, distinct speech, a clean reputation, a settled account, and a cool quiet evening.

title: 情 · feeling, affection, situation
desc: The heart radical beside the phonetic 青: the movements of the heart. From that one image grows feeling and mood, affection and love, and the wider sense of a situation or state of affairs.

title: 全 · whole, complete, entire, all
desc: Enter, and find the jade flawless. From that image of unblemished jade grows everything whole and complete: the entire set, the intact and unbroken, and the adverb that sweeps up all of it at once.

title: 容 · to contain, to allow, appearance
desc: A roof over a valley: the space that holds. To contain, to tolerate, the face one shows, and the easy in rongyi.

title: 如 · like, as, if, according to
desc: A woman speaking and a mouth complying: from following a command grew the great comparison-and-condition word. 如 is how Chinese says like, as, for example, and if.

title: 社 · society, an association, the god of the soil
desc: The altar radical beside the earth: a shrine to the god of the soil and the community that gathered around it. From that image grow society itself, the many kinds of association and agency, and the ancient soil-and-grain spirits that once stood for the state.

title: 声 · sound, voice, tone, reputation
desc: A chime-stone struck before a listening ear. From that image grow the everyday word for sound and voice, the tone of speech, and the wider sense of making something known: a declaration, a reputation, a name.

title: 实 · real, solid, true, actual
desc: A roof over a house full of goods. From that image of a full dwelling grows everything substantial: the real and the true, the solid and sturdy, the actual practice that gets things done, and the ripened fruit.

title: 世 · world, age, generation, lifetime
desc: A pictograph traditionally read as three tens joined together, the span of thirty years that makes one generation. From that root grow the four faces of 世: the generation that succeeds the one before, the lifetime or the life to come, the era stacked from many lives, and the wider world of human society in which all of it unfolds.

title: 首 · head, first, chief, a measure word for songs and poems
desc: A drawn head, with hair above an eye, and from it the senses of first, foremost, chief, leader, and the classifier you count songs and poems with. 首 is its own radical.

title: 题 · topic, question, problem, to inscribe
desc: The head-radical character behind every exam question and discussion topic. From the leaf or head of a thing grows the question to solve, the theme to discuss, and the act of inscribing a poem.

title: 通 · to go through; to connect; general; fluent
desc: The walk-movement radical drives a path through every obstacle, giving 通 a single character that covers passage, communication, expertise, and the ordinary general state of things.

title: 头 · head, top, end, chief, noun-suffix
desc: The head, and from it the top of a hill, the end of a street, the start of a thing, the chief of a group, and the toneless tag on a hundred everyday nouns. The simplified 头 stands for traditional 頭.

title: 望 · to gaze afar, to hope, reputation
desc: A person on a mound looking into the distance, with the moon above: from that raised gaze grow three senses. To gaze and look afar (眺望, 望远镜, 张望), to hope and expect (希望, 期望, 盼望, 失望), and reputation or prestige (名望, 威望, 声望). As a coverb it can even mean toward, like 朝 or 向.

title: 武 · martial, military, valiant
desc: The foot radical 止 carrying a dagger-axe 戈: the soldier on the march, and the older reading that to wield arms well is finally to halt them. From 武力 armed force to 武术 martial arts to 威武 powerful and dignified, the character holds the whole world of strength wielded with discipline.

title: 物 · thing, object, matter, being
desc: An ox under a phonetic, once the word for varicolored cattle, that broadened into the whole world of things: every object, all matter, the myriad creatures, and even a person as a figure.

title: 向 · direction, toward, to face, all along
desc: A window opening in a wall, facing one way. From that image grows the whole field of orientation: the direction a thing points, the preposition toward a target, the inclination of a heart, and the sense of all along, up to now.

title: 形 · shape, form, to appear, to compare
desc: The character for visible form: shape and figure, the body as form, the act of taking shape and being described, and the lay of a situation. A pictophonetic compound built on the pattern-strokes radical 彡.

title: 性 · nature, character, sex/gender, the -ness/-ity suffix
desc: The heart radical carrying the sense of innate nature: what a thing is born to be. From that core grow the four faces of 性: a persons disposition or character, sex and gender, the property or quality of a thing, and the productive abstract suffix that turns adjectives into -ness and -ity nouns.

title: 阳 · sun, bright, the yang principle
desc: A sunlit mound: the simplified 阳 sets a hill beside the sun. From that bright south slope grow the sun itself, the active masculine half of the cosmos, and the place names that face the light.

title: 业 · occupation, industry, undertaking, study
desc: A notched rack for hanging bells and chimes, then the work hung upon it. From that frame grows the whole field of doing: the trade one practices, the industry one builds, the cause one devotes a life to, the coursework one masters, and in Buddhist thought the karma one accrues.

title: 因 · cause, reason, because of, to follow
desc: A person resting inside an enclosure, the mat one lies on. From that image of lying-upon comes the basis one builds on, then the cause behind an effect and the because that links the two.

title: 音 · sound, tone, news
desc: A mouth with a sound marked inside it. From that image grow the words for sound and music, for the way a syllable is pronounced, and for tidings carried from afar.

title: 应 · ought, should; (yìng) to respond, to answer, to handle
desc: A high-frequency polyphone with two readings. As yīng it means ought to or should; as yìng it means to respond, to answer, to adapt, and to handle. The tone tells you whether the sense is obligation or response.

title: 于 · at, in, to, than (the classical preposition)
desc: The workhorse preposition of formal Chinese. 于 marks where, when, toward whom, and against what a thing is measured, and it is bound into a long list of everyday disyllables like 由于, 终于, and 等于.

title: 主 · master, host, main, to advocate
desc: A lamp flame steady on its stand: the central light that grew into the master of a household, the main thing among many, the one who decides, and the Lord of a faith.

title: 本 · root, origin, this, a book
desc: A tree with its root marked: the character for where a thing comes from. From root grows origin, the fundamental, one's own, the principal sum, and the bound volume you hold in your hand.

title: 部 · part, section, ministry, measure word
desc: The right-side city-mound radical marks an administrative division. From that grows the whole family of parts and wholes: a section of something, a government ministry, a military unit, and the measure word counted out for films, machines, and phones.

title: 菜 · vegetable, dish, cuisine
desc: Plants gathered to be eaten. From the picked greens grows a whole table: the vegetable, the cooked dish, the regional cuisine, and the slangy put-down for anyone weak at a task.

title: 常 · constant, ordinary, often
desc: A long banner of cloth that came to mean what endures: the constant and the lasting, the ordinary and the common, and the things that happen again and again.

title: 成 · to become, succeed, accomplished
desc: A halberd standing guard over a finished task. From that image grows the whole field of completion: to become, to succeed, to accomplish, the ready-made and the mature, and even the colloquial yes that settles a matter.

title: 词 · word, term, diction, the sung lyric
desc: Speech beside a phonetic 司: the unit we call a word, the wording a speaker chooses, and the classical lyric form that grew up beside regulated verse to be sung to set tune-patterns.

title: 第 · the ordinal prefix, rank, mansion
desc: Bamboo over younger-brother, an image of things laid out in sequence. From it grows the prefix that turns a count into an order, plus the older senses of examination rank and grand residence.

title: 点 · dot, point, a little, o'clock
desc: From a single dot of ink the character spreads into points and decimals, into the hours of the clock, into ordering food and lighting a flame, and into the small quantity that softens a sentence.

title: 动 · to move, to act, to stir
desc: Force applied to a thing sets it in motion. From that one idea grow the words for sport and activity, for the stirred heart, for the drive that pushes a machine or a life forward, and for the verb itself.

title: 法 · law, method, the Dharma
desc: Water against the level mark. From that image of fair, flowing measure grows the whole field of 法: the law and the court, the method and the way of doing a thing, and the Buddhist Dharma itself.

title: 方 · square, direction, method
desc: One glyph that runs from the literal square to the cardinal directions, to the place a thing sits, to the method by which it is done. The geometry of orientation and approach.

title: 非 · not, wrong, un-
desc: Two wings spreading in opposite directions: from that image of opposition grows the great negator. Not and non-, the line between right and wrong, and the un- prefix that turns a word against itself.

title: 分 · to divide, minute, point, cent
desc: A knife splitting a thing in two. From the cut grows everything that comes in parts: the minute on the clock, the point on a test, the cent in your pocket, and the act of separating itself.

title: 个 · the universal measure word, individual
desc: The general-purpose measure word that counts almost anything, and the root of individual. From the bamboo-stalk tally grew the everyday classifier 一个 and the words for individual, personality, and build.

title: 汉 · the Han river, dynasty, people, and a man
desc: A river that named a dynasty, and a dynasty that named a people. From the water of 汉水 grew 汉族 the Han ethnicity, 汉语 and 汉字 the Chinese language and script, and 好汉, the brave fellow.

title: 候 · to wait, time, season, climate
desc: A person standing watch beside the road. From the figure of one who waits and watches grows the everyday word for when (时候), the act of awaiting (等候), and the long rhythm of the weather (气候).

title: 花 · flower, to spend, patterned
desc: A plant caught in its transformed, blooming state: the flower, the act of spending money or time, and the patterned, fancy, or blurred. One glyph that runs from the garden to the wallet to the dazzled eye.

title: 话 · words, speech, talk, language
desc: Speech beside a tongue: the everyday character for spoken words. From it grow talking and conversation, the telephone, a dialect or standard language, and the topics and sayings people pass around.

title: 欢 · joy, merry, to be pleased
desc: A breath of open delight: the hand and the open mouth that make laughter. From this glyph come joy and merriment, to like and to welcome, and the lively, high-spirited mood.

title: 回 · to return, to turn back, a time
desc: Two squares nested like a coiling eddy. The character for coming back: returning home, turning around, replying, and counting the times a thing happens.

title: 记 · to remember, to record, a mark
desc: Speech set beside the self: the act of fixing something so it will not be lost. From that image grow three senses: to remember, to write down, and the mark left behind.

title: 间 · space between, interval, room
desc: Sunlight in the crack between two doors: the character for the space between things. From that gap grow time, the middle ground, the human world, and the room you count one by one.

title: 教 · to teach, teaching, religion
desc: A hand with a rod beside a child at the lesson. From that scene of instruction grows a wide field: to teach and educate, to teach a skill in the spoken jiao reading, and the teaching that became the word for religion.

title: 进 · to enter, to advance, to take in
desc: A foot on the road and a bird that only ever walks forward. From that image grows everything that moves ahead and moves in: to enter, to advance, to progress, to carry out, and to take goods in.

title: 经 · classic, scripture, to pass through, warp threads
desc: The lengthwise warp threads strung on a loom, the structural through-lines that hold a fabric together. From that image grow the canonical classic, the act of passing through, and the running of an enterprise.

title: 理 · principle, reason, to manage, texture
desc: The veins running through a piece of jade, the lines a carver follows when cutting. From that grain grows everything ordered: the inner pattern of things, principle and reason, and the work of putting a matter in order.

title: 门 · door, gate, family, field
desc: A picture of a two-leaf gate. From the swinging doors grow the gateway, the household behind them, the school or trade you enter, and the measure word for whole courses of study.

title: 面 · face, surface, side
desc: A pictograph of a face inside its outline that opened outward into surfaces, sides, and aspects, became a measure word for flat things, and in simplified script swallowed the separate character for flour and noodles.

title: 然 · so, thus, the -ly manner suffix
desc: A character that once meant to burn and was borrowed for the abstract sense so, correct, this-is-how-it-is. Today it builds the connectives 然后 and 然而, the conjunctions 当然 and 虽然, and rides as a -ly suffix on words like 忽然 and 突然.

title: 事 · matter, affair, thing-that-happens
desc: The character for an affair, a matter, a thing that happens. From an ancient pictograph of a hand holding the implements of office, it became Chinese for everything abstract that occupies us: business, jobs, incidents, and the everyday "no problem."

title: 太 · too, extremely, highest, grand
desc: The character 大 (big) with one extra dot, pushing big past its limit into too-much. From that excess grow the everyday too, the highest and grandest, the sun, and the supreme pole of Taiji.

title: 体 · body, substance, to experience
desc: The person beside the root: the body as a person's base. From the physical body grow substance and system, the whole as against the part, and the act of grasping a thing by living through it.

title: 同 · same, together, with
desc: Voices joined under one cover: the character for sameness and shared ground. From it grow the words for being alike, doing things together, and the people who share your role, your class, your cause.

title: 外 · outside, outer, foreign, besides
desc: A diviner reading the shells at the wrong hour, off the normal schedule. From that image grows everything beyond the boundary: the outside, the outer surface, the foreign land, and the relatives on the mother's side.

title: 问 · to ask, to inquire, to ask after
desc: A mouth at the gate, asking. From that image grow the everyday verb to ask, the noun for a question or problem, the warm act of asking after someone, and the stern act of holding to account.

title: 喜 · joy, to like, happy events
desc: A festive drum sounding above an open mouth: the sound of joy and the smiling mouth that answers it. From this image grow the words for liking, delight, and every happy occasion, above all the wedding.

title: 系 · to connect, system, department
desc: A hand holding silk threads. From that image of holding strands together come the great connecting words of modern Chinese: the system, the relationship, the link, the university department, and the colloquial act of tying a knot.

title: 现 · to appear, present, now
desc: The luster of jade coming into view. From that glint of something becoming visible grows the whole vocabulary of appearing, of the present moment, and of what is ready and on hand.

title: 相 · mutual, appearance, to examine, minister
desc: An eye examining a tree. From that act of looking grow two readings: level-tone xiang, the mutual that binds two sides face to face, and falling-tone xiang, the appearance you look at, the looking itself, and the minister who looks over the realm.

title: 样 · shape, kind, manner, sample
desc: A word once rooted in wood that grew into the language of appearance and kind: how a thing looks, what type it is, the sample held up as a model, and the everyday this-way and how of manner words.

title: 意 · meaning, intention, the wish of the mind
desc: Sound over heart: 意 is what the heart means before it is spoken. From that image grows meaning and significance, intention and willingness, and the notions of attention, satisfaction, and the unexpected.

title: 正 · upright, correct, exactly, in the midst of
desc: A foot halting squarely on the target line. From that image grows everything straight and correct: the upright, the standard, the exact moment, and the ongoing right-now.

title: 重 · heavy, important; again, to repeat
desc: A figure bearing a heavy load. From that weight grows everything that carries gravity: the heavy, the important, the grave. Read again as chóng, the same load comes back, layered and repeated.

title: 子 · child, seed, Master
desc: A picture of a swaddled infant that grew into one of the busiest characters in the language: a child and a son, the honorific for a Master, the empty noun-suffix on a thousand words, and the seed of a thing.

title: 自 · self, from, naturally
desc: A picture of a nose, the thing an ancient speaker pointed at to mean me. From that gesture grows the self, the source a thing comes from, and the sense of a thing acting of its own accord.

title: 作 · to do, to make, to compose
desc: A person setting something in motion. From the act of beginning grows the whole vocabulary of doing, making, and composing: the job you work, the work you create, and the role you act out.

title: 楚辞 · Songs of Chu
desc: The shamanistic southern voice that gave Chinese literature its second pole: visionary, romantic, and inconsolably exiled.

title: 鲁迅 · Lu Xun
desc: The writer who looked at traditional Chinese society and saw cannibalism, and the complicated, unresolvable legacy he left behind.

title: 山水画 · landscape painting
desc: Chinese landscape painting encodes a theory in its name: 山 (mountain, yang, permanent) and 水 (water, yin, changing) in dynamic tension. A space to inhabit in the imagination, not a view to frame.

title: 水墨画 · Ink-Wash Painting
desc: Where the brush meets philosophy: five tones of ink, the art of leaving space, and landscapes that are not about landscape at all.

title: 唐诗 · Tang Poetry
desc: Li Bai, Du Fu, and the golden age of regulated verse.

title: 篆刻 · Seal Carving
desc: The art of the name: bronze to stone, dynasty to dynasty, two schools of carvers, and the small red square that authenticates everything.

title: 低 · low; to lower; to bow down
desc: A person stooping: the phonetic 氐 gives the sound while the human radical supplies the posture, and together they built one of the most culturally loaded words in modern Chinese.

title: 佛 · Buddha, the awakened
desc: The character that carried an entire worldview across the Silk Road: etymology, Buddhism, the 佛-family of compounds.

title: 感 · to feel, to resonate
desc: Feeling, perception, gratitude, and the cosmology of sympathetic resonance.

title: 家 · home, family
desc: House, family, school of thought, nation (国家): the fractal of belonging.

title: 可 · can; may; worth; quite
desc: A two-stroke mouth character whose ancient sense of affirming breath became the pivot of permission, capability, and worth in classical and modern Chinese.

title: 空 · empty, sky, void; in vain
desc: A cave with the work of hollowing inside it. The character that names the open sky, the empty room, the wasted afternoon, and the Buddhist śūnyatā at the heart of Chan.

title: 龙 · dragon, the imperial symbol
desc: China's most powerful mythic creature: benevolent, not fearsome; the emperor's emblem and the Chinese people's self-described totem.

title: 你 · you
desc: The everyday second-person pronoun whose formal twin 您 embeds 心 (heart) directly into the character: address with warmth.

title: 其 · its, that, their
desc: A winnowing basket that became the pronoun holding classical Chinese together: the silent 'its' behind thousands of literary phrases.

title: 山 · mountain, hill, sacred peak
desc: Three peaks rising from the earth: the oldest pictograph and the axis of Chinese sacred geography.

title: 思 · to think, to miss, thought
desc: The field of the mind above the heart: thinking as cultivation, longing as thought turned inward.

title: 他 · he, him; another
desc: 他 was gender-neutral for a millennium until 她 was coined in 1917 to solve a translation problem that Classical Chinese had never needed to solve.

title: 天 · sky, heaven, day
desc: Heaven as moral authority, weather, time, and the ground of 天命 the Mandate of Heaven.

title: 万 · ten thousand; myriad; all
desc: 万 is the Chinese hyperbole unit. Where English reaches for millions, Chinese reaches for 万 to express the immeasurable, because the written number 10,000 originally meant scorpion.

title: 我 · I, me, myself
desc: The character for 'I' began as a toothed bronze halberd: the assertive grip of a weapon became the grammatical mark of a self.

title: 心 · heart, mind
desc: The radical at the root of all feeling, and the Chinese conception of thought itself.

title: 也 · also; too; classical particle
desc: A pictograph that lost its original image entirely and became one of the most load-bearing particles in classical Chinese: the gavel at the end of every verdict.

title: 以 · by means of; using; because; in order to
desc: A classical Chinese preposition and conjunction so versatile that it anchors half the grammar of formal Chinese: the word that turns one thing into the means, standard, or cause of another.

title: 义 · righteousness, duty, justice
desc: The Confucian virtue of doing what is morally right, and the simplification that erased a sheep, a self, and the entire picture of what righteous form looks like.

title: 语 · language, speech, words
desc: Speech radical plus the phonetic 吾 (I, me): the character for language carries the self within it, encoding the idea that language is the medium through which the self speaks to the world.

title: 雨 · rain
desc: The oracle bone shows rain falling from the sky: one of the most transparent pictographs in the script, and the radical that organizes all Chinese weather.

title: 之 · of, going, this: the classical connective
desc: The most-written character in classical Chinese: a possessive particle, pronoun, and verb fossilized into pure grammar.

title: 知 · to know; knowledge
desc: 知 = arrow + mouth: knowledge as the swift, target-hitting utterance, and in Wang Yangming, the act of knowing is inseparable from the act of doing.

title: 字 · character, written word
desc: The character that names itself, and the whole system of 汉字.

title: 重阳节 · Double Ninth Festival
desc: The festival named for two nines produced one of the Tang dynasty most memorized poems, and a linguistic trick that lets urban dwellers eat a cake instead of climbing a mountain.

title: 称呼 · Forms of Address
desc: In Chinese, how you address someone is not a formality. It is a precise statement of how you understand the relationship between you.

title: 口语连接词 · Conversational Connectors
desc: The discourse markers that make spoken Chinese sound natural: buying time, opining, hedging, redirecting, agreeing, and exiting a conversation without abruptness.

title: 姓名 · Names
desc: Family name first, given name second: the structure, meaning-making, and social logic of Chinese personal names.

title: 语言 · The Language
desc: Characters, vocabulary, grammar. The building blocks of written and spoken Chinese.

title: 被 · the passive
desc: Agentive passive, unmarked passive, and the adversarial connotation.

title: 的 · 得 · 地 · the three de's
desc: Attribution, result complement, and adverbial marker: distinguished once and for all.

title: 就 vs. 才 · sooner vs. later
desc: The timing and emphasis pair: speaker attitude encoded in one syllable.

title: 所 · classical nominalizer and passive marker
desc: The function word that turns verbs into noun phrases, and has been doing so since Confucius quoted it in the Analects.

title: 因为…所以 · because…therefore
desc: The causal conjunction pair: 因为 states the cause and 所以 announces the result, forming a two-clause logical structure that Chinese uses more explicitly than English.

title: 着 · the continuous aspect marker
desc: Three distinct jobs: holding a state, linking two actions, and commanding attention. All from a single particle that beginners collapse into one.

title: 改革开放 · Reform and Opening Up
desc: Deng Xiaoping's 1978 pivot that transformed China from a closed command economy into the world's second largest economy in four decades.

title: 汉朝 · The Han Dynasty
desc: Why Chinese call themselves 汉人: the dynasty that defined the civilization.

title: 汉朝 · The Han Dynasty
desc: The dynasty that named the Chinese people and script: 400 years of empire, the Silk Road, Confucian statecraft, and Sima Qian writing history from prison.

title: 明朝 · The Ming Dynasty
desc: The Great Wall rebuilt, Zheng He's voyages, and the inward turn.

title: 秦始皇 · The First Emperor
desc: Unification, standardization, and the terror that made China.

title: 秦朝 · The Qin Dynasty (221–206 BCE)
desc: Fifteen years of imperial rule, fifteen centuries of imperial inheritance. The Qin unified the warring states, standardized writing, currency, and roads, built the first long wall, burned the books, and collapsed under the weight of its own apparatus.

title: 唐朝 · The Tang Dynasty
desc: The cosmopolitan golden age: poetry, Buddhism, and the Silk Road.

title: 夏商周 · The Three Dynasties
desc: The legendary and early historical origins of Chinese civilization.

title: 周朝 · The Zhou Dynasty
desc: The longest dynasty in Chinese history and the philosophical seedbed of Chinese civilization: where the Mandate of Heaven was born, Confucius lived, and nearly every idea that shaped imperial China was first argued.

title: 孔子 · Confucius
desc: His life, the Analects 论语, and the civilization he shaped.

title: 老子 · Laozi & the Daodejing
desc: The 81 chapters, wu wei 无为, and the paradox at the heart of Daoist thought.

title: 理学 · Neo-Confucianism
desc: Zhu Xi, the Great Ultimate 太极, and the Song-Ming synthesis.

title: 荀子 · Xunzi
desc: Human nature as bad: ritual and education as correction.

title: 王阳明 · Wang Yangming and the School of Mind
desc: Wang Yangming broke Neo-Confucianism open: instead of investigating external things to reach moral truth, he turned inward and declared that the moral mind already knows, and that knowing and acting are one indivisible movement.

title: 易经 · The Book of Changes
desc: The oldest and most cryptic of the Chinese classics: a manual of divination, a philosophy of change, and a map of the universe encoded in 64 hexagrams.

title: 庄子 · Zhuangzi
desc: The butterfly dream, Cook Ding, and Daoist freedom from convention.

title: 城隍 · The City God
desc: Every Chinese city had a City God who served as its divine magistrate, managing the dead and the living with the same bureaucratic precision as any imperial official.

title: 佛教 · Buddhism in China
desc: Two thousand years of transmission, transformation, and sinicization.

title: 民间信仰 · Folk Religion
desc: Kitchen gods, city gods, and the living popular religion beneath Buddhism and Daoism.

title: 历法 · The Lunisolar Calendar
desc: Neither purely solar nor purely lunar, the Chinese calendar has kept farmers, physicians, and dynasties synchronized with the cosmos for three thousand years.

title: 算盘 · The Abacus
desc: Before the electronic calculator, a bead frame and trained fingers could outrun early computers on everyday arithmetic.

title: 天干地支 · Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches: the 60-year cycle
desc: A combinatorial timekeeping system the Shang scribes used in 1250 BCE to date their divination sessions, and that Chinese people still use to name years, hours, and contract parties today.

title: 五行 · Five Phases
desc: The Qin dynasty dressed its armies in black and flew black banners because its theorists believed they ruled under the Water phase: this is how consequentially the Five Phases shaped Chinese history.

title: 星宿 · Chinese Constellations
desc: China mapped the entire sky independently of Greece: 1,464 stars, 28 lunar mansions, and four mythological guardians that divided the cosmos long before Ptolemy.

title: 笔画 · strokes: the building blocks of Chinese characters
desc: Every Chinese character is built from a small set of standard strokes written in a prescribed order. Stroke count determines dictionary order; stroke order determines how a character looks when written by hand.

title: 部首 · radicals: the indexing keys of Chinese characters
desc: Every Chinese character belongs to a radical family. Radicals are the organizing principle of dictionaries, the structural DNA of characters, and the fastest shortcut to guessing what an unfamiliar word means.

title: 长城 · the Great Wall
desc: A series of fortification systems built across multiple dynasties, whose most visible sections are Ming-era brick: not the continuous ancient rampart of popular imagination.

title: 东西 · things
desc: East-west as the word for 'stuff': a window into directional cosmology.

title: 江山 · rivers and mountains, the realm
desc: The classical Chinese word for the nation: not a territory but a landscape; not a state but a living geography that dynasties rose and fell to possess.

title: 君子 · the exemplary person
desc: The Confucian moral ideal that replaced aristocratic birth with cultivated virtue as the basis of social authority: anyone who does the work of 仁义礼智信 qualifies.

title: 历史 · history
desc: The character for historian shows a hand holding a brush over a vessel: in ancient China, the scribe who held the brush held power.

title: 拼音 · the romanization system for Mandarin
desc: Pinyin is the official romanization of Mandarin: the system that maps Chinese sounds to the Latin alphabet. It is a pronunciation guide, not a writing system, and it does not replace characters.

title: 仁 · humaneness, benevolence
desc: The supreme Confucian virtue: the quality of genuine care for other people that holds civilization together.

title: 人间 · the human world; the mortal realm
desc: The world of people: where karma plays out, where flowers fade in April, and where the only beings who can hear the Dharma are born.

title: 社会 · society
desc: The word for society that China borrowed from Japan, which had borrowed the characters from China: a compound forged at the altar of the earth.

title: 神明 · gods, spirits, deities; divine intelligence
desc: The generic term for any deity in the Chinese religious world: and, in classical philosophy, the luminous intelligence that distinguishes the divine from the merely powerful.

title: 诗词 · Chinese poetry
desc: Poetry stood at the center of Chinese civilization for two thousand years: the primary medium for expressing emotion, demonstrating education, and participating in the social life of the literati class.

title: 天命 · the Mandate of Heaven
desc: The political and cosmological concept that legitimized three thousand years of Chinese dynasty: heaven's appointment of the rightful ruler.

title: 天人合一 · Heaven and humanity as one: the unity of cosmic and human order
desc: The organizing claim of Chinese cosmology: Heaven and humanity are not separate domains, and human flourishing depends on alignment with the natural order.

title: 天下 · all under heaven
desc: The pre-nation-state Chinese political imagination: the civilized world.

title: 阴阳 · yin and yang
desc: The binary engine of all classical Chinese thought.

title: 智慧 · wisdom; prajna
desc: 智慧 brings together Confucian moral discernment and Buddhist prajna under one compound: two traditions, one word, different objects of knowing.

title: 中医 · Traditional Chinese Medicine
desc: Two thousand years of systematic medical thought: qi, yin-yang, the Five Elements, acupuncture, and the living tradition that treats the person, not the disease.

title: 八 · eight; the luckiest number and the eight trigrams
desc: Eight is the most coveted number in modern China through its near-homophony with 发 fā (to prosper), and the classical foundation of the eight trigrams that structure the Yijing.

title: 黑 · black, darkness, and the illicit
desc: Black on the surface, but the live sense is moral: the black market, the underworld, the hacker. The color that names everything that operates out of sight.

title: 很 · very; the empty intensifier
desc: 很 is the word for very, but its strangest job is doing nothing: Chinese needs a degree adverb before a plain adjective, and 很 fills that slot so quietly that 我很好 means simply I am fine, not I am very well.

title: 红 · red, the color of luck and celebration
desc: The cultural keystone color: weddings, New Year, the red envelope, and a century of revolutionary politics all run through this one character.

title: 九 · nine; the imperial number and the highest of the yang
desc: Nine is the largest single digit and the highest yang number, reserved for the emperor and the heavens: nine dragons, nine gates, the Nine-Five supreme position, the ninth heaven.

title: 两 · two (of); a pair; the tael, the other word for two
desc: 两 is the two used before measure words, the two of quantity and pairing, as opposed to 二 the two of counting and order, a distinction that is one of the first real puzzles a learner meets.

title: 零 · zero; raindrops, the fractional remainder, and the late invention of nothing
desc: Zero began as falling raindrops and the leftover odd remainder, taking on the meaning of mathematical nothing only late, the placeholder that Chinese numerals long managed without.

title: 六 · six; the six directions; a smooth and lucky number
desc: Six closes space into the six directions (the four compass points plus up and down) and, through its near-homophony with 流 liú (to flow), became a number for things going smoothly.

title: 念 · to recite, to keep in mind, to miss
desc: 念 holds the present moment 今 over the heart 心: to keep something in mind, to recite aloud, to long for what is absent. The 念 of 念佛 recitation, 想念 longing, and the single thought-moment of Buddhist psychology.

title: 七 · seven; the rhythm of mourning, festival, and the soul
desc: Seven measures the cycles of death and renewal in Chinese culture: the seven-day periods of mourning, the seventh-night lovers' festival, and the seven emotions of the heart.

title: 千 · thousand; a vast, uncountable many
desc: Thousand is the order of magnitude where a precise count gives way to poetic vastness: a thousand miles, a thousand autumns, ten thousand changes, the number that means simply too many to count.

title: 四 · four; the four directions; the homophone of death
desc: Four organizes the Chinese world into quarters, the four directions, four seas, four seasons, yet its near-homophony with 死 sǐ (death) makes it the most avoided number in modern China.

title: 它 · it; the non-human third person
desc: 它 began as a picture of a snake and once meant other; in the twentieth century it was reassigned to the non-human third person, completing the homophonous 他/她/它 triad that exists only in writing.

title: 完 · to finish; to be whole
desc: 完 means both whole and finished, and the bridge between them is intact completeness; its most important job is as a result complement, the 完 that ends 吃完, 做完, and 看完.

title: 五 · five; the organizing number of correlative cosmology
desc: Five is the center plus the four directions, the number that completes the Chinese cosmos: five phases, five colors, five tones, five flavors, five viscera, all keyed to one master grid.

title: 雪 · snow, whiteness, and vengeance
desc: Rain over a sweeping hand: snow is the precipitation you can hold. The same character means dazzling white and, by a buried metaphor, to wipe clean an old grievance.

title: 阴 · the shaded slope, the lunar, the covert
desc: The shadow half of the cosmos and the everyday word for an overcast day. From the dark side of a hill grew the lunar calendar, the hidden plot, and time itself as light and shade.

title: 最 · most; the superlative marker
desc: 最 is the single word that pushes any adjective to its limit: the -est of English, the most of comparison, the marker that turns 好 into 最好 and 后 into 最后.

title: 做 · to do, to make, to act as
desc: 做 is the everyday verb for doing and making, a late character built to carry the work that 作 had grown too literary to do, and the two still split the labor between them.

title: 曹操 · The Warlord-Poet
desc: The man who held the dying Han together by force, wrote some of the finest poetry in the language, and became Chinese literature's most magnificent villain.

title: 玄奘 · The Pilgrim of the West
desc: The Tang monk who crossed the deserts to India for the scriptures, studied sixteen years, and came home to translate them: the historical figure behind Journey to the West.

title: 阿弥陀佛 · Amitābha Buddha
desc: 阿弥陀佛 is the Buddha of Infinite Light and Life who presides over the Western Pure Land, and his name is itself the central practice: to recite 南无阿弥陀佛 is the simple path of Pure Land devotion, open to everyone.

title: 皇帝 · emperor
desc: The title the First Emperor invented in 221 BCE by welding together 皇 (august sage-king) and 帝 (high god), and how it differs from 王 king, 君 sovereign, and 天子 the Son of Heaven.

title: 时代 · era, age
desc: The word for a historical era or age, built from 时 (time) and 代 (generation), and how it differs from 时期 a period, 年代 a decade, 时候 a moment, and 现代 modern times.

title: 现代 · modern times
desc: The word for the modern era, built from 现 (present, manifest) and 代 (generation, age), how Chinese history slices time into 古代 / 近代 / 现代 / 当代, and how 现代 differs from 现在 now.

title: 跟 · with; and; to follow
desc: The everyday coverb for "with" and conjunction for "and", how the 跟…一起 and 跟…说 patterns work, the original verb "to follow", and how 跟 differs from 和, 同, and 与.

title: 离 · away from; distance
desc: The coverb for distance and separation: the A 离 B + distance pattern for "how far", the verb sense "to leave / part from", and how 离 differs from 从 and 到 in marking space and time.

title: 往 · toward; to head for
desc: The directional coverb for "toward", the 往 + direction + verb pattern, the verb sense "to go / in the past", and how 往 differs from 向 and 朝 for facing and motion.

title: 为什么 · why
desc: The neutral question word for cause and reason, how to answer it with 因为 or 为了, and how a plain 为什么 differs from the surprised 怎么 and the purpose-asking 为了什么.

title: 怎么 · how, in what way; why
desc: The all-purpose question word for manner and reason: how to do something, what is wrong, and the surprised "how come," plus how 怎么 differs from 为什么 and 怎么样.

title: 然后 · then; after that
desc: The everyday sequence word for "then, after that," the 先…然后… frame for ordering steps, its overuse as a spoken filler, and how it differs from 接着, 后来, and 于是.

title: 一定 · definitely; certainly
desc: The everyday word for "certainly, definitely," covering both confident prediction and firm resolve, the 一定要 (must) pattern, and how it differs from 肯定, 必须, and 一定会.

title: 一起 · together
desc: The everyday word for "together," the 跟…一起 frame for joint action, the "in one place" sense, the "altogether" use of 一起, and how it differs from 一块儿, 一同, and 一共.

title: 终于 · finally, at last
desc: The adverb for "finally, at last," used when something long-awaited or hard-won comes to pass, where it sits in a sentence, and how it differs from 最后, 总算, and 到底.

title: 多少 / 几 · how many, how much
desc: The two question words for quantity: 几 for small countable numbers and 多少 for larger or unknown amounts, why 几 needs a measure word and 多少 may skip it, and how to ask prices and ages.

title: 可能 · maybe, possible
desc: The all-purpose word for possibility, working as adverb, adjective, and noun, and how it differs from 也许, 或许, 大概, and the modal 会.

title: 应该 · the modal "should"
desc: The modal verb for "should, ought to," covering both moral obligation and confident inference, and how it differs from 得, 要, and 必须.

title: 一下 · the verb-softener
desc: The verbal-quantity word that makes an action brief and casual, how verb + 一下 softens a request, and how it differs from verb reduplication and from the time-word 一会儿.

title: 帮助 · to help
desc: The everyday word for help, both verb and noun, and how it differs from the lighter 帮 and the separable 帮忙 (to do a favor).

title: 工作 · work, job
desc: The everyday word for work, both the activity and the job itself, and how it differs from 上班 (to go to work), 职业 (occupation), and 事业 (career).

title: 其实 · actually
desc: The everyday adverb for "actually, in fact," used to correct an impression or reveal the real situation, and how it differs from 实际上, 事实上, and 本来.

title: 现在 · now
desc: The everyday word for now, where it sits in a Chinese sentence, and how it differs from 目前 (at present), 此刻 (this very moment), and 如今 (nowadays).

title: 希望 · to hope
desc: The everyday word for hope, both the verb and the noun, and how it differs from 想 (to want), 愿意 (to be willing), 盼望 (to long for), and 期待 (to look forward to).

title: 一会儿 · a short while
desc: The everyday word for a little while, how it marks both a short duration and the near future, and how it differs from the verb-softener 一下 and from 等会儿.

title: 红楼梦 · Dream of the Red Chamber
desc: The 18th-century novel that many call the greatest in the Chinese language: the slow decline of a great family, a doomed love among the young, and a sense that all the beauty and luxury of the world is a passing dream.

title: 三国演义 · Romance of the Three Kingdoms
desc: The 14th-century novel that turned the wars after the Han into the great epic of Chinese loyalty and cunning. Sworn brothers, a god-like strategist, and the maxim that the realm long divided must unite.

title: 水浒传 · Water Margin
desc: One hundred and eight outlaws, each driven from honest life by a corrupt officialdom, gather at the marsh of Liangshan to rob the rich and defy the state. The 14th-century novel of righteous banditry and brotherhood.

title: 西游记 · Journey to the West
desc: A Buddhist monk, a rebellious immortal monkey, a glutton pig, and a river demon travel west for the scriptures. The 16th-century novel of pilgrimage, magic, and mischief that gave the world the Monkey King.

title: 给 · to give, for, and to
desc: The verb "to give," the coverb that marks a recipient or beneficiary ("for/to"), and a colloquial passive marker, all from one character.

title: 还是 / 或者 · "or" in questions vs. statements
desc: Chinese splits English "or" in two: 还是 offers a choice in a question, 或者 offers an alternative in a statement. Using the wrong one is a classic error.

title: 吗 · the yes-no question particle
desc: The simplest way to ask a question in Mandarin: add 吗 to the end of a statement. Plus how it differs from A-not-A questions and from 呢 and 吧.

title: 一点儿 / 有点儿 · a little
desc: The classic confusion pair: 有点儿 comes before an adjective and leans negative ("a bit too…"), while 一点儿 comes after and is neutral ("a little more").

title: 一样 / 像 · same and similar
desc: How to say two things are the same (A 跟 B 一样) or alike (A 像 B), and how this differs from the unequal comparison with 比.

title: 在 · location, existence, and the progressive
desc: One of the busiest words in Mandarin: the verb "to be at," the location coverb "at/in," and the progressive marker for ongoing action.

title: 兵马俑 · The Terracotta Army
desc: Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, each with a different face, buried to guard the First Emperor in death. A farmer digging a well found them in 1974, and the silent army became the most astonishing archaeological discovery of the century.

title: 三国 · The Three Kingdoms
desc: After the Han collapsed, China split into three rival states: Wei, Shu, and Wu. The sixty years of their wars produced the most beloved cast of heroes, traitors, and strategists in Chinese history.

title: 史记 · Records of the Grand Historian
desc: Sima Qian wrote the founding work of Chinese historiography under the shadow of his own mutilation: a vast history from the legendary Yellow Emperor to his own Han dynasty, and the model every later dynastic history would follow.

title: 隋朝 · The Sui Dynasty
desc: A short, ferocious dynasty that reunified China after nearly four centuries of division, dug the Grand Canal, and laid the institutions the glorious Tang would inherit, then burned itself out in a single generation.

title: 道德经 · Daodejing
desc: Eighty-one short chapters of paradox and indirection that became the foundational text of Daoism and one of the most translated books in human history. The way that can be spoken is not the constant way.

title: 孙子兵法 · The Art of War
desc: Thirteen terse chapters on conflict, attributed to the strategist Sun Wu, that became the oldest and most influential military treatise in the world. The supreme art is to subdue the enemy without fighting.

title: 觉得 · to think, to feel
desc: The everyday verb for giving an opinion or impression, and how it differs from the more formal 认为 and from 想 (to want / to think over).

title: 朋友 · friend
desc: The everyday word for friend, and the rich web of relationship terms (好朋友, 男朋友, 交朋友) built around it.

title: 时候 · time, moment
desc: The everyday word for a point in time, and the indispensable 的时候 ("when") pattern that every learner needs.

title: 问题 · question, problem
desc: One word for both "question" and "problem", and the everyday phrases (没问题, 有问题, 出问题) built from it.

title: 喜欢 · to like
desc: The everyday verb for liking, and how it differs from loving (爱), enjoying (喜爱), and being willing (愿意).

title: 知道 · to know
desc: The everyday verb for knowing a fact, and how it differs from 认识 (to be acquainted with) and 了解 (to understand deeply).

title: 阿弥陀经 · The Smaller Amitabha Sutra
desc: The shorter Pure Land sutra: ~1,800 characters in which the Buddha describes Amitābha's Western Pure Land to Śāriputra and names the practice of single-minded recollection of the Buddha's name. The daily-recitation text of Pure Land Buddhism.

title: 佛经 · Buddhist Scriptures
desc: The core Mahāyāna sutras the site presents in full: the Chan canon (心经, 金刚经, 坛经) and the Pure Land canon (阿弥陀经, 无量寿经, 观无量寿经). Each linked here gets its own page with full text, line-by-line audio, pinyin gloss, English translation, and commentary.

title: 心经 · The Heart Sutra
desc: The Heart Sutra: 260 characters that condense the entire Prajñāpāramitā teaching of emptiness. Translated by Xuanzang in 649 CE; chanted daily across China, Japan, Korea, and Vietnam ever since. The full text, line by line, with audio, gloss, and commentary.

title: 必须 · must, have to (the obligation modal)
desc: 必须 is the strongest of the everyday modal verbs of obligation: a non-negotiable requirement that the speaker presents as not-up-for-discussion.

title: 般若 · prajñā; the Buddhist wisdom that sees emptiness
desc: 般若 is the specific Buddhist wisdom that perceives the emptiness of self and phenomena: not knowledge, not cleverness, but the realization that dissolves clinging at its root.

title: 论语 · The Analects of Confucius
desc: The Analects: a thin book of recorded conversations and sayings that became the most quoted text in East Asian civilization, the entry point to Confucian thought, and the textbook of imperial education for two thousand years.

title: 涅槃 · Nirvana; the extinction of craving and the end of rebirth
desc: 涅槃 is the Buddhist soteriological terminus: the extinction of the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion, and the cessation of the karmic cycle that they fuel.

title: 文明 · civilization; cultivated and refined
desc: 文明 names both a state of cultivated life (literacy, ritual, the refined arts) and the global concept of civilization. The two meanings share a single Chinese word, and the doubling is the whole story.

title: 命 · life, fate, command
desc: A mouth speaking an order: 令 above, 口 inside. The character that holds together three of the heaviest words in Chinese: life, destiny, and the command from above.

title: 跨 · to stride; to span; to bestride
desc: The character of the long stride: a foot-radical verb that reaches from "step over a threshold" to "span an era" to the modern policy vocabulary of cross-border, cross-industry, cross-cultural everything.

title: 跑 · to run; to flee; to operate
